# **Overview**

Calculating AA T1D PRS, research GRS2, and clinical package GRS2  in TEDDY.

For all, the starting raw genetic data is in PLINK format at:
  raw/TEDDYarrays_v2/additional_data/Norris_SNP_exome_masked

TOPMed R3 imputation was done in the script:
  explore_matprot/teddy_risk_scores/run_teddy_tm_imp.Rmd
  
1000G imputation was done in the script:
  explore_matprot/risk_scores/1_run_teddy_1000g_imp.Rmd
  
Michigan HLA imputation was done in the script:
  explore_matprot/teddy_risk_scores/run_teddy_mich_hla_imp.Rmd
  
For both imputations, an HWE filter of 1e-20 was used for the MHC region of
chr6. See details in topmed_imputation repo.

**SDS 20240822: This script has been cleaned up, but an original version of**
**the report has been saved as 2_calc_teddy_risk_scores_all_version.html,**
**which more thoroughly documents all mappings tested before we understood**
**the TOPMed R2 update to R3 around December 2023 was the problem.**

To troubleshoot, the original report:

+ Checked TOPMed R3 imputation output overlap with the GRS2 calculated
  previously in TEDDY using 59 SNPs in
  [PMID 32770166](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7556983/#SD1)
  + The haplogenotype portion of the score was very difficult to map based on
    TEDDY's description of excluding non-eligible haplogenotypes. See more on
    that in Immunogenetics_T1D/documentation/daisy_teddy_hla_eligibility.xlsx
    and Maternal_Protection/documentation/teddy_daisy_risk_score_documentation.xlsx
  + The non-haplogenotype portion of the score was also difficult to map as
    TEDDY did not include a mapping of there SNPs to the original score. Was
    able to map most by direct match, but couldn't resolve all SNPs.
  
2. Mapped the GRS2 TOPMed R2 map subset to TEDDY 59 SNPs to the TEDDY TOPMed R3
  imputation results with very little overlap - 41 SNPs. Only 8 SNPs mapped
  from the HLA imputation results.
  
3. Finally, switched to 1000G GRS2 map from the HLA PRS toolkit and imputed
  TEDDY to 1000G phase 3 version 5, population = EUR. Much better overlap, and
  that was the only GRS2 score calculated for TEDDY in this report.

**1. AA T1D PRS (PMID 30659077)**

For SNPs in HLA on chromosome 6, using HLA imputed data. For other two SNPs,
using TopMed imputed data.

PRS SNPs from paper are in hg19. TOPMed results are in hg38 and HLA imputation
results are in hg19.

**2. Research GRS2**

Calculating GRS2 in DAISY based on PMID 30655379 & process followed for DAISY
(see Rmd calc_daisy_grs2). Referencing
[GitHub](https://github.com/sethsh7/hla-prs-toolkit) for HLA haplotype pipeline.

When running the hla-prs-toolkit, using mapping and rank files provided by the
GitHub:

+ T1DGRS67_TOPMED_mapping.txt
+ HLADQ_USAEuropean_Klitz.txt

The toolkit also provides an Excel file (T1DGRS67_TOPMED_hg38.xlsx) with all
haplogenotypes and SNPs in the GRS2, with the mapping of RSIDs to chr:pos:ref:alt.
Use this to add RSIDs to PLINK file and confirm REF/ALT encoding.

Not sure whether to use TOPMed imputed input or HLA imputed input, but GitHub
and paper mention TOPMed imptued data.

Imputed TEDDY to 1000G (reference panel 1000G phase 3 version 5, population =
EUR), and scored with the HLA PRS toolkit map for 1000G imputation.

**3. Clinical Package GRS2**

Not calculating at this time. When calculated in DAISY, scale seemed off, and
the publication is not yet out so hard to verify results.

#### **Get Overlap**

Also merging in the chr6 variants here, even though I will likely use chr6
variants imputed by Michigan HLA imputation where possible instead of these.

*Joining by position since clean .pvar has chr:pos:ref:alt varIDs.*

```{r}
table_tm <- left_join(
  table, tm_hg38, by = c("pos_hg38" = "POS",
                         "Chr" = "#CHROM"))

table_tm %>% dplyr::select(SNP, Chr, pos_hg19, Effect, pos_hg38, REF, ALT, INFO)

```

Of the five SNPs on chr6, three are present in the TOPMed imputed data with
R2 > 0.97. The single chr11 SNP is also found with R2 > 0.97, and the chr17 SNP
is found twice - once as typed and one as imputed.

Likely will not use any of these chr6 SNPs if possible - see what SNPs can pull
from the HLA Michigan imputation results below.

For the chr17 SNP, think better to use the typed SNP than the imputed
SNP. Not sure if there's a more systematic way to do think in PLINK/bcftools
(for all duplicate positions, remove the imputed SNP and keep the typed SNP),
but for these risk scores, think can just rename all variant IDs to 
chr:pos:ref:alt, which will allow me to select the typed SNP when filtering.

### **With HLA Imp**

#### **Liftover HLA Imputation**

Michigan HLA imputation with 4-digit multi-ethic panel v2 (most up to date panel
at the time of this report). Results are in hg19, which matches PRS SNPs, but
want to liftover to hg38 since will calculate score with TOPMed imputation
results in hg38.

2024-05-20 11:38:00 [INFO]  Total entries: 22733
2024-05-20 11:38:00 [INFO]  Failed to map: 1693

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}
conda activate crossmap-bcftools-osx64
code_dir="/Users/slacksa/repos/explore_matprot/teddy_risk_scores/"

bash ${code_dir}/liftover.sh \
  data/genetics/teddy/mich_hla_imp/imputed/chr6.dose.vcf.gz \
  raw/genome_maps/hg19ToHg38.over.chain.gz \
  raw/genome_maps/hg38.fa.gz \
  data/genetics/teddy/mich_hla_imp/imputed
```


*To note: current results are as is - no cleaning  by MAF or Rsq since want to*
*preserve lower MAFs in HLA region and will be checking Rsq by hand here. But*
*do we want a cleaned stable version of the dataset?*

#### **Get Overlap**

**Join by RSID:**

```{r}
table_hla <- left_join(
  table %>% dplyr::filter(Chr == 6),
  hla_chr6_hg38,
  by = c("SNP" = "ID"))

table_hla %>% dplyr::select(SNP, Chr, pos_hg19, Effect, POS, REF, ALT, INFO)
```

**Join by position (hg38):**

```{r}
table_hla_pos <- left_join(
  table %>% dplyr::filter(Chr == 6),
  hla_chr6_hg38,
  by = c("pos_hg38" = "POS"))

table_hla_pos %>% dplyr::select(SNP, Chr, pos_hg19, Effect, pos_hg38, REF, ALT, INFO)
```

Matches are the same regardless of joining by RSID or by position.

Three of the five SNPs are present in the HLA imputed data all with an
R2 > 0.99.

The SNP rs34303755 was also not present in the TOPMed imputed data, so will
need a proxy SNP.

The SNP rs9271594 was present in the TOPMed data, so will use the TOPMed data
as input for the SNP instead of getting a proxy.

## **Proxy SNPs**

Used ldlink NIH LD Proxy tool in ASW population (Americans of African Ancestry
SW USA), check that consistent with all populations. Showing proxy results in
build GRCh37. Showing the same results that were used for DAISY since the
same SNP that was not found here was not found in the DAISY data.

### **Proxy SNP 1**

One SNP not found in any of our imputed data: rs34303755.

```{r}
orig_1 <- "rs34303755"

table %>% dplyr::filter(SNP == orig_1)
```

#### **LDProxy**

Loading the same LDProxy results that were downloaded for DAISY, using result
for ALL populations, since DAISY risk scores reports showed fairly similar.

```{r}
proxy_all_filt <- proxy_all %>% dplyr::filter(R2 > 0.8) %>% arrange(desc(R2))
head(proxy_all_filt)
```

#### **Check for Lemon's Proxy SNP (rs9268923) in LDProxy Results**

Screenshot with information from Maizy from Lemon:

![](background/teddy_risk_scores/aa_7_snp_prs_from_lemon.png)

*More detail about Lemon's proxy SNPs in Excel table at*
*background/teddy_risk_scores/proxy_snp_comparison.xlsx.*

**Show Lemon's proxy SNP in ALL:**

```{r}
proxy_1 <- "rs9268923"
proxy_all %>% dplyr::filter(RS_Number == proxy_1)
```

Proxy R2 is almost 0.9. MAF is 0.2931, which is slightly higher than that
reported by the PRS score.

Since this was the SNP used as proxy for DAISY, think makes sense to use again
for TEDDY. Note correlated alleles: A=C, C=T.

#### **Check for Lemon's Proxy SNP in TEDDY Data**

**Check for Lemon's proxy SNP in HLA imputation:**

```{r}
hla_chr6_hg38 %>% dplyr::filter(ID == proxy_1)
```

Marked as type with high ALT_Frq (0.51).

#### **Check Effect Alleles**

**Original PRS SNP:**

*To note: Effect.Allele column is effect allele frequency.*

```{r}
table %>% dplyr::filter(SNP == orig_1)
```

Effect allele = C.

**Lemon's proxy in HLA-imputed data:**

```{r}
hla_chr6_hg38 %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, POS, REF, ALT, INFO) %>%
  dplyr::filter(ID == proxy_1)
```

They do not match - paper says original PRS SNP should have effect allele
frequency 0.22, but Lemon's proxy SNP in TEDDY data has AF = 0.51 (and this is
for a typed SNP). The AF was similarly high for DAISY as well.

**LDProxy Correlated SNPs:**

```{r}
proxy_1_info <- proxy_all %>% dplyr::filter(RS_Number == proxy_1)
proxy_1_info
```

Correlated alleles: A=C, C=T. So A in original SNP is like counting C for proxy
SNP and C in original SNP is like counting T for proxy SNP. Since effect
allele = C for original SNP, want to count T for proxy SNP.

```{r}
table$Effect.Allele[table$SNP == orig_1]
```


**Check dbSNP:**

+ original PRS SNP: rs34303755
  + ref:alt A:C
  + alt freq all pops: 0.22
  + AA freq: 0.15
+ Lemon's proxy: rs9268923
  + ref:alt C:T
  + alt freq all pops: 0.32
  + AA freq: 0.23
  
Allele frequency in TEDDY data is higher (0.48) than in all reference pops, but
wouldn't we actually expect this for a cohort with higher T1D? This was the
same for DAISY.

**Conclusion:** Use this proxy SNP to be consistent with DAISY and Lemon. 

## **Final Plan**

### **Overview**

Data for 4/5 chr6 SNPs (3 matching PRS + 1 proxy) will be from HLA Imputation.
The final chr6 SNP and chr11 and 17 SNPS will be from TOPMed imputation. Score
will be calculated after liftover of genetic data to hg19, so need to use
variant IDs in hg19.

```{r, message = F}
# Prep HLA Imp
table_hla_for_merge <- table_hla %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(INFO)) %>%
  dplyr::select(SNP, Chr, pos_hg19, Effect, Weight, POS, REF, ALT, INFO) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "hla_imp")

# Prep TM - keeping SNPs from HLA Imp when SNPs found in both
dup_rsid <- table_tm$SNP[duplicated(table_tm$SNP)]
table_tm_for_merge <- table_tm %>%
  dplyr::filter(!(SNP == dup_rsid & str_detect(INFO, "IMPUTED"))) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(INFO)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!SNP %in% table_hla_for_merge$SNP) %>%
  dplyr::select(SNP, Chr, pos_hg19, Effect, Weight, pos_hg38, REF, ALT, INFO) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "tm_imp")

# Merge
table_tm_for_merge <- table_tm_for_merge %>%
  dplyr::rename(POS = pos_hg38)
table_tm_hla <- full_join(
  table_hla_for_merge,
  table_tm_for_merge)


# Add proxy
table_proxy <- table %>%
  dplyr::filter(!SNP %in% table_tm_hla$SNP)
table_proxy$SNP_proxy = proxy_1
table_proxy$Correlated_Alleles = proxy_1_info$Correlated_Alleles

table_proxy_hla <- inner_join(
  table_proxy, hla_chr6_hg38, by = c("SNP_proxy" = "ID")) %>%
  dplyr::rename(POS_proxy = POS,
                REF_proxy = REF,
                ALT_proxy = ALT,
                INFO_proxy = INFO) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    SNP, Chr, pos_hg19, Effect, Weight, SNP_proxy, POS_proxy,
    REF_proxy, ALT_proxy, Correlated_Alleles, INFO_proxy) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "hla_imp_proxy")

# Merge
table_tm_hla_proxy <- full_join(table_tm_hla, table_proxy_hla)

# Add chr:pos:ref:alt ID col

  dplyr::mutate(var_id = case_when(
    !is.na(SNP_proxy) ~
      paste0(Chr, ":", POS_proxy, ":", REF_proxy, ":", ALT_proxy),
    is.na(SNP_proxy) ~
      paste0(Chr, ":", POS, ":", REF, ":", ALT)))

datatable(table_tm_hla_proxy)

table_tm_hla_proxy_tm_filt <- table_tm_hla_proxy %>%
  dplyr::filter(source == "tm_imp" | source == "tm_imp_proxy") %>%
  dplyr::select(var_id)
```

Files for filtering genetic files written out below using the above column

### **Combine Genetic Data**

Using HLA imputation and TOPMed imputation both in hg38.

#### **Prep for Merge**

**TOPMed:**

Concatenate all TOPMed files, update variant IDs to chr:pos:ref:alt, & extract
only the desired variants.

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}
conda activate bcftools-osx64

# Make file_list for input into bcftools concat
ls /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_tm_imp/imputed_clean/chr*_clean.vcf.gz | \
  sort -V > \
  /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_tm_imp/imputed_clean/tmp_tm_file_list.txt

# Concatenate VCFs
bcftools concat \
  --file-list /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_tm_imp/imputed_clean/tmp_tm_file_list.txt \
  --output-type z \
  --output /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_tm_imp/imputed_clean/chr_all_concat.vcf.gz

# Index
tabix /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_tm_imp/imputed_clean/chr_all_concat.vcf.gz

# Cleanup
rm /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_tm_imp/imputed_clean/tmp_*

```

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}
# Make plink file and set all varIDs
plink2 \
  --vcf /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_tm_imp/imputed_clean/chr_all_concat.vcf.gz \
  --id-delim \
  --set-all-var-ids @:#:\$r:\$a --new-id-max-allele-len 100 \
  --make-pgen \
  --out /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_tm_imp/imputed_clean/chr_all_concat
```

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}

plink2 --pfile /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_tm_imp/imputed_clean/chr_all_concat \
  --extract data/teddy_risk_scores/aa_7snp/genetics/tm_imp_snps_hg38.txt \
  --export vcf 'bgz' \
  --out data/teddy_risk_scores/aa_7snp/genetics/tm_imp_hg38

tabix data/teddy_risk_scores/aa_7snp/genetics/tm_imp_hg38.vcf.gz
```

**HLA Imp:**

Update ID format & extract desired variants.

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}
conda activate bcftools-osx64

plink2 --pfile data/genetics/teddy/mich_hla_imp/imputed/chr6.dose_38 \
    --set-all-var-ids @:#:\$r:\$a --new-id-max-allele-len 100 \
    --make-pgen --out data/genetics/teddy/mich_hla_imp/imputed/tmp_chr6
  
plink2 --pfile data/genetics/teddy/mich_hla_imp/imputed/tmp_chr6 \
    --export vcf 'bgz' \
    --extract data/teddy_risk_scores/aa_7snp/genetics/hla_imp_snps_hg38.txt \

# Index

# Clean up
```

Needed to use -a to allow "First coordinate of the next file can precede last
record of the current file."

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}
  data/teddy_risk_scores/aa_7snp/genetics/tm_imp_hg38.vcf.gz \
  data/teddy_risk_scores/aa_7snp/genetics/hla_imp_hg38.vcf.gz \
  --output-type z \

  --make-pgen --id-delim \
  --out data/teddy_risk_scores/aa_7snp/genetics/merge_hg38

```

## **PRS Calculation**

Using PLINK2 --score option to calculate PRS.

First, need to make input file with allele and score. The input file must have
exactly one line per scored allele. Variant IDs are read from column #i and
allele codes are read from column j, where i defaults to 1 and j defaults to i+1.
By default, a single column of coefficients is read from column #k, where k
defaults to j+1. To specify multiple columns, use --score-col-nums.

Create score file with Effect.Allele column and proxy SNP counting T (see above
section on proxy SNP).

```{r}
# Prep proxies correlated alleles
get_corr_allele <- function(proxy_corr, effect_allele) {
  # Split the string by comma
  corrs <- unlist(strsplit(proxy_corr, split = ","))
  
  # Find the part that starts with var
  corr_want <- corrs[grepl(paste0("^", effect_allele, "="), corrs)]
  allele_want <- gsub("^.+=", "", corr_want)
  
  return(allele_want)
}

# Test
# get_corr_allele(proxy_1_info$Correlated_Alleles, table$Effect[table$SNP == orig_1])

# Format output for input into PLINK --score
score <- table_tm_hla_proxy %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    effect_allele = case_when(
      SNP_proxy == proxy_1 ~
        get_corr_allele(proxy_1_info$Correlated_Alleles,
                        table$Effect[table$SNP == orig_1]),
      is.na(SNP_proxy) ~ Effect)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(prs_aa_7snp = Weight) %>%
  dplyr::select(var_id, effect_allele, prs_aa_7snp)

# Show here, write out at end
head(c, n = 10)

```

Calculate score in PLINK.

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}
plink2 --pfile data/teddy_risk_scores/aa_7snp/genetics/merge_hg38 \
  --score data/teddy_risk_scores/aa_7snp/scoring/aa_7snp_score_input.txt \
  cols=+scoresums header-read \
  --out data/teddy_risk_scores/aa_7snp/scoring/teddy_aa_7snp_prs
```

**By Position:**

```{r}
  map_tk_1kg,
  kg_hg19_all %>% dplyr::mutate(
    chrpos = gsub(":[[:alpha:]]+:[[:alpha:]]+$", "", SNP)),
  by = c("POSITION_DBSNP151" = "chrpos"))
```

If check imputed files after cleaning (MAF 0.01, Rsq 0.3), there are
`r kg_hg19_no_map_count` SNPs that are not found in the data. However, if check
before any cleaning, all SNPs are found, `r kg_hg19_all_no_map_count` do not
map! This makes sense since this map was intended to be used with 1000G
imputation.

Do either the low Rsq or low MAF include the TEDDY non-eligible HLA-DQ markers?

low MAF or low Rsq don't tag any of the 5 TEDDY-eligible DR types (1, 3, 4, 8,


**Conclusion:** Calculate score removing the DQ SNPs with low Rsq, not finding
proxies for them since they are tag SNPs. For the non-DQ SNPs with low Rsq,
find proxy SNPs. Leave SNPs with low MAF as is.

*TODO: confirm this with Randi! And ask if want to leave or remove the low-MAF*
*DQ SNPs?*

## **Proxy SNPs - 1000G with 1000G Imputed Data**

Using the LDLink R tool to batch search. Getting proxy SNPs only for non-
haplogenotype tag SNPs. Searching in hg19, all populations, with chr:pos IDs.

Getting proxy SNPs for non-HLA DQ SNPs with low Rsq (Rsq <= 0.3):

```{r}
# Get list to search for proxies
# Get those not found
map_tk_1kg_kg_hg19_all_low_rsq <- map_tk_1kg_kg_hg19_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(Rsq <= 0.3) %>%
  dplyr::filter(SCORE != "NA") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(chrpos = paste0("chr", gsub(":[[:alpha:]]+:[[:alpha:]]+$", "", SNP)))

map_tk_1kg_kg_hg19_all_low_rsq %>%
  dplyr::select(COMPONENT, RSID, SCORE, chrpos)

proxy_search_kg = map_tk_1kg_kg_hg19_all_low_rsq$chrpos

```

*TO NOTE: LDLink chunk is very slow. Run once interactively then re-load results.*

```{r eval = F}
# Run search
LDproxy_batch(proxy_search_kg,
    pop = "ALL",
    r2d = "r2",
    token = "f9898ebc08dd",
    append = TRUE,
    genome_build = "grch37")

# Results loaded above as proxy_result_kg
```

Results were found for SNPs:

```{r}
unique((proxy_result_kg$query_snp))
```

Now, map these to imputed data and see if any good proxies (LD R2 >= 0.8) for
either/both:

*To note: many-to-many warning is expected since queried SNPs could have*
*overlapping results.*

```{r}

# Filter to LD R2 >= 0.8 before map with proxy results
proxy_result_kg_0.8 <- proxy_result_kg %>%
  dplyr::filter(R2 >= 0.8)

proxy_result_kg_kg_hg19_all <- inner_join(
  proxy_result_kg_0.8,
  kg_hg19_all %>% dplyr::mutate(chrpos = paste0("chr", gsub(":[[:alpha:]]+:[[:alpha:]]+$", "", SNP))),
  by = c("Coord" = "chrpos"),
  suffix = c("_proxy", "_1kg_imp"))
```


```{r}
proxy_result_kg_kg_hg19_all_filt <- proxy_result_kg_kg_hg19_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(!Coord %in% proxy_search_kg)

proxy_result_kg_kg_hg19_all_filt %>%
  dplyr::select(query_snp, RS_Number, Coord, R2, MAF_proxy, MAF_1kg_imp, Rsq, Genotyped)
```

Only one SNP for each has R2 >= 0.8, and both have low Rsq.

**Conclusion: will not get proxies for these SNPs.**

## **Final Plan - 1000G with 1000G Imputed Data**

All 67 GRS2 SNPs from the 1000G map were found in the unfiltered 1000G-imputed
data. However, `r kg_hg19_all_low_rsq_count` SNPs mapped with Rsq <= 0.3, and
`r kg_hg19_all_low_maf_count` mapped with MAF <= 0.01. Going to score the SNPs
with low MAF as is, tried to get proxy SNPs for the `r length(proxy_search_kg)`
SNPs with low Rsq that were not HLA-DQ SNPs, but there were none availbe with
LD R2 >= 0.8 and reasonable imputation R2. Not including the low Rsq HLA-DQ
SNPs, since also confirmed they are not marking TEDDY eligibility SNPs (see
Excel sheet in documentation folder). 

```{r}
map_tk_1kg_final <- map_tk_1kg_kg_hg19_all %>%
  dplyr::mutate(score = case_when(
    Rsq < 0.3 ~ "no",
    Rsq >= 0.3 ~ "yes"
  ))

datatable(map_tk_1kg_final %>%
            dplyr::select(score, COMPONENT, RSID, A1,
                          A2, SCORE,
                          SCORE_ALLELE, SNP, MAF, Rsq, Genotyped))

map_tk_1kg_final_score <- map_tk_1kg_final %>%
  dplyr::filter(score == "yes")
```


## **PRS Calculation - 1000G with 1000G Imputed Data**

### **Prep Genetic Data**

Since using unfiltered imputation results, files are very large. As a first
step, make combined file with just the `r sum(map_tk_1kg_final$score == "yes")`
that will be used for calculating both parts of the score.

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}
mamba activate bcftools-osx64

# Make tmp dir for intermediate files
mkdir /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_1000g_imp/tmp

# Extract SNPs from each chr one at a time
for chr in {1..22}
do
  plink2 --vcf /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_1000g_imp/imputed/chr${chr}.dose.vcf.gz \
    --extract data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_snps_hg19.txt \
    --out /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_1000g_imp/tmp/tmp_grs2_chr${chr} \
    --export vcf bgz
done

# Make file_list for input into bcftools concat
ls /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_1000g_imp/tmp/*.vcf.gz | sort -V > \
  /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_1000g_imp/tmp/tmp_grs2_file_list.txt

# Concatenate VCFs
bcftools concat \
  --file-list /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_1000g_imp/tmp/tmp_grs2_file_list.txt \
  --output-type z \
  --output data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_hg19.vcf.gz

# Make PLINK file
plink2 --vcf data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_hg19.vcf.gz \
  --make-pgen --set-all-var-ids @:#:\$r:\$a \
  --out data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_hg19

# Clean up
rm -r /Users/slacksa/temp_data/maternal_protection/teddy_1000g_imp/tmp


```

Also write out a version of the data with RSIDs as variant IDs (instead of
chr:pos:ref:alt) for the haplogenotype calculation.

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}

plink2 --pfile data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_hg19 \
  --update-name data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_haplogeno_snps_hg19.txt \
  --extract data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_haplogeno_snps_hg19.txt \
  --make-bed \
  --out data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_haplogeno_hg19

```

### **HLA Haplogenotypes**

#### 1. Check AFs of Effect Allele

```{r}
map_tk_1kg_final_score %>%
  dplyr::filter(SCORE == "NA") %>%
  dplyr::select(COMPONENT, A1, A2, `Freq_UKB(A1)`,
                `Freq_UKB(A2)`, SCORE_ALLELE, `REF(0)`, `ALT(1)`, MAF)
```

All REF/ALT alleles encoded in the same way. Score allele is alt allele in
TEDDY data. In general, TEDDY MAF is lower than UKB reported MAF, except for
DQ81 and DQ25. This makes sense - DQ81 marks DR4 and DQ25 marks DR3.

#### 2. Step 1 of the HLA PRS toolkit

Using same conda environment set up for scoring in DAISY: hla-prs-toolkit with
numpy==1.21.5 pandas==1.3.5 docopt==0.6.2

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}
conda activate hla-prs-toolkit
code_dir="/Users/slacksa/repos/explore_matprot/teddy_risk_scores"

python ${code_dir}/hla-prs-toolkit/1_plink2call.py \
    --bfile data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_haplogeno_hg19 \
    --mapping ${code_dir}/hla-prs-toolkit/Tools/Snps/1000G/T1DGRS67_1000G_mapping.txt \
    --rank  ${code_dir}/hla-prs-toolkit/Tools/Reference/HLADQ_USAEuropean_Klitz.txt

```

This step creates imp_1000g_haplogeno_hg19_Categorical.txt.

#### 3. Step 2 of the HLA PRS toolkit

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}
conda activate hla-prs-toolkit
code_dir="/Users/slacksa/repos/explore_matprot/teddy_risk_scores"

python ${code_dir}/hla-prs-toolkit/2_cat2scores.py \
    --cat data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_haplogeno_hg19_Categorical.txt \
    --score ${code_dir}/hla-prs-toolkit/Tools/Scores/T1DGRS67_allele_scores.txt

```

This step creates imp_1000g_haplogeno_hg19_Categorical_Scored.txt

### **Non-Haplogenotype SNPs**

#### 1. Check AFs of Effect Allele

Filter to rows where SCORE_ALLELE != A2 & SCORE_ALLELE != A1:

(Checked that A1 always equals TEDDY REF and A2 always equals TEDDY ALT.)

```{r}
map_tk_1kg_final_score %>%
  dplyr::filter(SCORE != "NA") %>%
  dplyr::filter(SCORE_ALLELE != A2 &
                  SCORE_ALLELE != A1) %>%
  dplyr::select(COMPONENT, A1, A2, `Freq_UKB(A1)`,
                `Freq_UKB(A2)`, SCORE_ALLELE, SNP, `REF(0)`, `ALT(1)`, MAF)

flip_grs2_1000g <- map_tk_1kg_final_score %>%
  dplyr::filter(SCORE != "NA") %>%
  dplyr::filter(SCORE_ALLELE != A2 & SCORE_ALLELE != A1) %>%
  dplyr::select(SNP)
```

For this SNP, the HLA PRS toolki map, the A1 and A2 listed are both different
from the SCORE_ALLELE. This SNP 6:32395942:C:T will not be scored by PLINK
--score as is. Strand flip in PLINK to update data coding to G:A, but variant
name will retain C:T.

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}

plink2 --pfile data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_hg19 \
  --make-bed --out data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/tmp_imp_1000g_hg19 \

plink --bfile data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/tmp_imp_1000g_hg19 \
  --flip data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/scoring_1000g/grs2_strand_flip.txt \
  --make-bed --keep-allele-order \
  --out data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_hg19_flip

rm data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/tmp_imp_1000g_hg19*

```


#### 2. Score with PLINK

Now, use PLINK --score to calculate the non-haplogenotype portion of the score.

The input file must have exactly one line per scored allele. Variant IDs are
read from column #i and allele codes are read from column j, where i defaults to
1 and j defaults to i+1. By default, a single column of coefficients is read
from column #k, where k defaults to j+1. To specify multiple columns, use
–score-col-nums.

```{r}
# Prep for write out of non-haplogenotype SNPs only
score_grs2_1000g <- map_tk_1kg_final_score %>%
  dplyr::mutate(effect_allele = SCORE_ALLELE,
                grs2 = SCORE,
                var_id = SNP) %>%
  dplyr::select(var_id, effect_allele, grs2) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!grs2 == "NA")
```

```{zsh engine.opts='-i', eval = F}
plink2 --bfile data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_hg19_flip \
  --score data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/scoring_1000g/grs2_score_input.txt \
    cols=+scoresums header-read list-variants \
  --out data/teddy_risk_scores/grs2/scoring_1000g/teddy_grs2_non_haplogeno

```



### **Merge Score**

Merge haplogenotype and non-haplogenotype parts of score.

HLA PRS toolkit: To generate a complete PRS (e.g. variants outside the HLA
region) you can then sum this component with regular allele scoring generated
using PLINK score function.

```{r}
grs2_kg_comb <- inner_join(
  grs2_kg_haplogeno, grs2_kg_nonhaplogeno,
  by = c("FID" = "#FID", "IID")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ID = gsub("^.+_", "", IID),
    FID = gsub("_.+$", "", IID),
    GRS2 = SCORE + grs2_SUM) %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, GRS2)

# Write out combined score at end of script

```


## **Check Score - 1000G with 1000G Imputed Data**

**Summary:**  Score calculated with 10 haplogenotype SNPs + 51 non-haplogenotype
SNPs = 61 total SNPs.

### **Score Distribution**

```{r}
grs2_kg_comb_pheno <- inner_join(
  grs2_kg_comb,
  pheno %>% dplyr::mutate(maskid = as.character(maskid)),
  by = c("ID" = "maskid"))

ggplot(grs2_kg_comb_pheno, aes(x = GRS2, fill = as.factor(t1d))) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "GRS2 by T1D Case/Control")
```

### **Weights and SNPs in Score**

All SNPs for the 1000G-calculated score were from the 1000G imputation results.

Weights for the non-haplogenotype SNPs that were and weren't scored:

```{r, warning = F, fig.height = 8}

map_tk_1kg_final_mod <- map_tk_1kg_final %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    POS = as.numeric(gsub("^.+:", "", SNP)),
    CHR = as.numeric(gsub(":.+$", "", SNP)),
    var_id = factor(SNP, levels = unique(SNP[order(CHR, POS, decreasing = T)])),
    SCORE = as.numeric(SCORE)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!SCORE == "NA")  # remove HLA-DQ

ggplot(map_tk_1kg_final_mod,
       aes(x = SCORE, y = var_id, fill = score)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("chr", CHR), x = -1), hjust = 0) +
  labs(
    y = "Variant ID (hg19)",
    fill = "Data Source"
  )
```




# **3. Research GRS2 - HLA & Non-HLA Versions**

Calculating version of the score without any HLA or HLA-DQ haplogenotype SNPs
for IDS 2024 poster. Partially motivated by
[PMID 30655385](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30655385/). Also calculating
version of the score with only HLA and HLA-DQ haplogenotype contributions.

## **Get SNP Lists**

```{r}
map_tk_1kg_final_score_non_hla <-map_tk_1kg_final_score %>%
  dplyr::filter(COMPONENT == "Non-HLA")
map_tk_1kg_final_score_hla <-map_tk_1kg_final_score %>%
  dplyr::filter(COMPONENT != "Non-HLA")
```

The non-HLA score will have `r nrow(map_tk_1kg_final_score_non_hla)` SNPs.
The HLA only score will have `r nrow(map_tk_1kg_final_score_hla)` SNPs - this
includes the same haplogenotype SNPs as in full score.

```{r}
# Make PLINK input to --score for by filtering previous file
score_grs2_1000g_non_hla <- score_grs2_1000g %>%
  dplyr::filter(var_id %in% map_tk_1kg_final_score_non_hla$SNP)
score_grs2_1000g_hla <- score_grs2_1000g %>%
  dplyr::filter(var_id %in% map_tk_1kg_final_score_hla$SNP)
```

## **Calculation - Non-Haplogenotype SNPs**

```{zsh eval = F}
plink2 --bfile data/teddy/risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_hg19_flip \
  --score data/teddy/risk_scores/grs2/scoring_1000g/grs2_score_input_non_hla.txt \
    cols=+scoresums header-read list-variants \
  --out data/teddy/risk_scores/grs2/scoring_1000g/teddy_grs2_non_haplogeno_non_hla

plink2 --bfile data/teddy/risk_scores/grs2/genetics_1000g/imp_1000g_hg19_flip \
  --score data/teddy/risk_scores/grs2/scoring_1000g/grs2_score_input_hla_only.txt \
    cols=+scoresums header-read list-variants \
  --out data/teddy/risk_scores/grs2/scoring_1000g/teddy_grs2_non_haplogeno_hla_only
```

## **Merge Score**

Only need to do this for HLA-only score.

```{r}
grs2_kg_comb_hla <- inner_join(
  grs2_kg_haplogeno, grs2_kg_nonhaplogeno_hla,
  by = c("FID" = "#FID", "IID")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ID = gsub("^.+_", "", IID),
    FID = gsub("_.+$", "", IID),
    GRS2 = SCORE + grs2_SUM) %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, GRS2)

# Also modify formatting to write out non HLA score
grs2_kg_comb_non_hla <- grs2_kg_nonhaplogeno_non_hla %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ID = gsub("^.+_", "", IID),
    FID = gsub("_.+$", "", IID),
    GRS2 = SCORE + grs2_SUM) %>%
  dplyr::select(ID, GRS2)

```
